axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Datadog observability data
(logs/metrics/traces/dashboards/monitors/incidents/security signals, etc.) as tools for agents.
The official docs' position: most tools query the Datadog backend directly without a model; a few semantic-search / natural-language-to-query tools
do use models hosted by Datadog's AI providers, and can be disabled org-wide.
axes.background:
The service lives on Datadog's side; session request-response, no background-listening semantics.
The official docs state that MCP usage information is collected (tool names/parameters/errors/user identifiers, excluding prompts and model reasoning), stored for 120 days.
axes.tools:
Grouped by **toolsets** (selected via the URL parameter ?toolsets=, default core): core (logs/metrics/traces/
dashboards/monitors/incidents/hosts/services/events/notebooks), alerting, apm (Preview),
cases, dbm, ddsql (Preview), error-tracking, feature-flags, llmobs, product-analytics,
networks, onboarding, security, software-delivery, synthetics, workflows; toolsets=all enables every GA group.
axes.context: No server-side cross-session memory — state lives on the Datadog platform itself; the official docs recommend trimming tools via toolsets to save context window.
axes.permissions:
**The permission surface is the core of this entry**: the official docs state plainly that the server forwards the authenticated user's own credentials to the Datadog API —
**RBAC / Data Access Control / log restrictions apply unchanged; the server cannot grant a user anything beyond their own access**.
Write actions require the corresponding permission (e.g. monitors_write), checked on every tool call; read-only users calling write tools get rejected.
Org admins can manage global MCP access and write capability in Organization Settings, and can enable an IP allowlist.
axes.fit:
Fits: coding/ops agents pulling live production context (logs/metrics/traces/incidents) while debugging,
debugging against real data inside the IDE.
Not a fit: GovCloud environments (officially stated incompatible); needing fully local offline (the remote line must reach Datadog;
the local binary is only a local auth shell — tools still live remotely).

mcp.scope:
A large read surface (logs/metrics/traces/dashboards/monitors/incidents etc., grouped by toolsets);
write actions (creating monitors, modifying cases, etc.) require the corresponding write permission, checked per call.
The official position: all MCP tool calls go into the Audit Trail (tool name/parameters/user/client),
plus two standard metrics, datadog.mcp.session.starts and datadog.mcp.tool.calls.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The complete tool list within each toolset (the official docs list group names and some tools, not enumerated item by item)
- Current rate-limit numbers (the official docs gave figures and state plainly they "may change"; per our D9 rule and snapshot discipline no specific numbers are stored)
- Windows support details of the local-binary line (the official docs give download guidance, not verified item by item)
related: Also the observability surface: Grafana is open-source and self-hostable; Datadog is closed-source hosted with credential pass-through.
Same-category contrast: Sentry focuses on error issues; Datadog is the full-stack observability platform surface.
